advances: Fixed positive polytopal fiber family and fixed cap count, at regular interior feasible budgets only. The optimized objective is the selected cover's hinge; no all-normal optimality or universal bound on its multipliers is inferred.

proof:
For $n\ge1$ attainment follows from dd9bb9379a876e89 on exactly the stated actual-fiber cover with continuous unit normals; for $n=0$ use that fact on the single base $0\in\mathbb Z$ and delete the ineffectual base coefficients. Feasibility is upward closed, so $J$ is an interval, and $v$ is nonincreasing. The functions $F_z$ are locally Lipschitz by uniform margin comparison. Cap masses are locally Lipschitz on the ambient neighborhood with $\lVert u_i\rVert$ bounded away from zero: in a bounded fiber only a slab of thickness $O(\lVert\delta p\rVert)$ changes membership, and its orthogonal projection area is uniformly bounded (equal to one in dimension one). The same holds for $s$ and $G=\max(0,\max_z(-F_z))$. Nonvertical cap boundaries are $\mu$-null, so dominated differentiation gives $\Psi_i\in C^1$ with differential $(Z_i,X_i,-c_i)$; dominated convergence gives continuity of these moments.

Clipped polytope volumes and first moments are semialgebraic. Intersect the fixed facet presentation with the cap inequality and enumerate candidate vertices by nonsingular systems of active rows. Each is a rational function of the coefficients on its nonzero determinant locus. Partition by the finite signs of feasibility, incidence and orientation determinants, clearing denominators on fixed sign cells; on each piece a fixed pulling triangulation gives finite rational formulas for volume and first moments, with zero contribution when the clipping is lower dimensional. Thus $\Psi_i=a_i\cdot Z_i+u_i\cdot X_i-b_ic_i$ is also semialgebraic. The graph of $F_z$ is semialgebraic by its defining min-max quantification over a fixed polytope. Quantifying feasibility and optimality describes the attained graph of $v$. Real quantifier elimination and one-variable piecewise $C^1$ regularity (Coste, [Introduction to O-minimal Geometry](https://perso.univ-rennes1.fr/michel.coste/polyens/OMIN.pdf), Theorems 1.13 and 6.7) give the finite exceptional set.

Subtract $G(p)$ from every $b_i$ to obtain $R(p)$. Every margin and hence each $F_z$ increases by exactly $G(p)$, so $R(p)$ is a cover, remains on the product of unit spheres, and $\lVert R(p)-p\rVert=\sqrt N G(p)$. At a minimizing cover $p_*$ of a regular budget, choose a local Lipschitz constant $A$ for $v$. Nearby covers satisfy $\Psi(p)+A(s(p)-\tau)_+\ge v(\tau)$ by optimality at $\tau$ or at $s(p)$, according as $s(p)\le\tau$ or $s(p)>\tau$. If $B$ is a local Lipschitz constant of this penalized objective, the repair bounds its decrease by $B\sqrt N G(p)$, giving an unconstrained local minimum after adding that last penalty, on the product of spheres. This also shows normality without any strict cap slack qualification.

To obtain exact sensitivity, if $s(p_*)=\tau$, use $f_0=\Psi-v(s)$ instead. This is locally Lipschitz because $s$ stays in a regular interval about $\tau$; it is nonnegative on nearby covers and vanishes at $p_*$. By the repair, $f_0+B_0\sqrt N G$ has a local minimum for a local Lipschitz constant $B_0$ of $f_0$. If $s(p_*)<\tau$, the minimizer is feasible at every budget just below $\tau$, forcing $v$ constant on a left interval by monotonicity and therefore $v'(\tau)=0$. In a neighborhood all covers stay below budget, so the same repair gives a local minimum of $\Psi+B_0\sqrt N G$.

Apply Clarke Fermat, sum, maximum and differentiable outer chain inclusions ([Clarke, Optimization and Nonsmooth Analysis, chapter 2](https://doi.org/10.1137/1.9781611971309.ch2)) in sphere charts. Equivalently pull back the ambient Clarke gradient sets by the differential of the smooth inclusion of the chart; the chain inclusion suffices. The smooth hinge enters with coefficient one. In the active budget case the $-v(s)$ term supplies $r_i=-v'(\tau)\omega_i'/M$ with nonnegative simplex weights $\omega_i'$ supported on $c_i=\tau M$. In the slack case take $r_i=0$. The $G$ term supplies nonnegative weights $\eta_z$ on active negative coverage gradients, possibly with weight on zero, with sum at most $B_0\sqrt N$. Use the consistent ambient cap-gradient construction in c343c9f3dc96957e, whose proof first establishes the representation for the unrestricted cap-mass function before imposing any minimizer conditions. Its projected regular section limits give a single dominated section measure per cap, and the section is contained in $L_i=0$. Use the coverage Clarke lemma above for the active gradients; the signs are negative because $G$ uses $-F_z$. The accepted minimax contact conditions retained in that lemma give $\lambda_i L_i=0$ and actual fiber support for every chosen pair. These steps also apply for $d=1$, where the continuous sphere has zero tangent dimension and the full continuous component is in its normal space.

Writing the ambient sum as normal to the product of spheres yields the first two stated balances from the free offset and base components, and
$$
X_i+r_i X_i^s-\sum_z\eta_zq_{zi}+\sigma_i u_i=0
$$
for some real $\sigma_i$. Pair this with $u_i$, add the base balance paired with $a_i$, and subtract $b_i$ times the mass balance, writing both balances as left minus right equal to zero. The cap integral is $\Psi_i$, the section integral vanishes on $L_i=0$, and each saddle contact term vanishes by $\lambda_i L_i=0$. Therefore $\sigma_i=-\Psi_i$, proving the last equation. The first two equations match the source and contact mass and base moments; no convex order is needed. The finite exceptional set also implies that any feasible cap ratio strictly below a given $\alpha\in(0,1)$ has an intermediate regular budget below $\alpha$.

statement:
Let $n\ge0,d,N\ge1$, let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be finite nonempty and let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be fixed full-dimensional compact polytopes. Write $S=\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$, with summed fiber volume $\mu$ and $M=\mu(S)$. For $N$ cap margins $L_i(z,x)=a_i\cdot z+u_i\cdot x-b_i$, $\lVert u_i\rVert=1$, let $H_i=\{L_i\ge0\}$, $c_i=\mu(S\cap H_i)$, $\Psi_i=\int (L_i)_+\,d\mu$, $\Psi=\sum_i\Psi_i$, $s=\max_i c_i/M$, and $F_z=\min_{x\in K_z}\max_i L_i(z,x)$. Let $J\subset(0,1)$ consist of budgets $\tau$ admitting a cover ($F_z\ge0$ for all $z$) with $s\le\tau$, and $v(\tau)$ be the minimum hinge. The minimum is attained, $J$ is upward closed in $(0,1)$, and $v$ is nonincreasing and $C^1$ locally on $\operatorname{int}J$ except at a finite set.

At every such regular budget and every minimizing cover there exist $r_i,\eta_z\ge0$ with $r_i(c_i-\tau M)=0$, $\eta_zF_z=0$, and $M\sum_i r_i=-v'(\tau)$. Set $Z_i=\int_{H_i} z\,d\mu$, $X_i=\int_{H_i} x\,d\mu$. For each cap use one consistent section measure $d\omega_i=\theta_{iz}\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}/\lVert u_i\rVert$ on each $K_z\cap\{L_i=0\}$, with $0\le\theta_{iz}\le1$ and $\theta_{iz}=1$ a.e. on proper sections, yielding moments $(S_i,Z_i^s,X_i^s)=\int(1,z,x)\,d\omega_i$. For every $z$ with $\eta_z>0$ there is a finite probability law on actual saddle pairs $(x,\lambda)$ for $F_z$. Let $p_{zi}=\int\lambda_i$ and $q_{zi}=\int\lambda_i x$ for that law. The stress has objective multiplier one and satisfies
$$
\begin{aligned}
c_i+r_i S_i&=\sum_z\eta_z p_{zi},\\
Z_i+r_i Z_i^s&=\sum_z\eta_z z p_{zi},\\
X_i+r_i X_i^s&=\sum_z\eta_z q_{zi}+\Psi_i u_i.
\end{aligned}
$$
In the tangent equation prior to eliminating the sphere normal, its multiplier is $-\Psi_i$. The section measure uses counting measure for $d=1$.
title: Regular budgets give normalized hinge stress for covers of actual polytopal fibers
